newsitem.title: GABON: Text of Gabon mini-summit declaration on Zaire.
newsitem.headline: Text of Gabon mini-summit declaration on Zaire.

text.p: Zaire's President Mobutu Sese Seko and fellow Central African presidents at a mini-summit in Gabon called for a peaceful resolution of Zaire's civil war.
Following is an unofficial Reuters translation of the declaration issued in French on Thursday.
LIBREVILLE DECLARATION

At the request of His Excellency Field Marshal Mobutu Sese Seko, President of the Republic of Zaire, and on the invitation of His Excellency El Hadj Omar Bongo, President of the Gabonese Republic, an extraordinary summit of Central African heads of state was held in Libreville on the 8th of May 1997.
Taking part at this summit were their Excellencies:
- Mr Mobutu Sese Seko, President of the Republic of Zaire,
- El Hadj Omar Bongo, President of the Republic of Gabon,
- Mr Teodoro Obiang Nguema Mbasogo, President of the Republic of Equatorial Guinea,
- Mr Idriss Deby, President of the Republic of Chad,
- Professor Pascal Lissouba, President of the Republic of Congo,
- Mr Ange-Felix Patasse, President of the Central African Republic,
- Mr Ferdinand Leopold Oyono, Minister of External Affairs, representing President Paul Biya of the Republic of Cameroon, current Chairman of the Organisation of African Unity (OAU).

The heads of state of Central Africa examined the evolution of the crisis in Zaire in light of the conclusions of the meeting between President Mobutu and Mr Laurent Desire Kabila, under the auspices of Mr Nelson Mandela, President of the South African Republic and Mr Mohamed Sahnoun, Special Representative of the United Nations and OAU on the 4th of May 1997 at Pointe Noire.
The heads of state of Central Africa have understood the exhaustive account that President Mobutu has given of the history of the Zairean crisis.

After a thorough exchange of views, the heads of state reaffirm their strong attachment to a negotiated political solution to the conflict and reject all recourse to violence as a means to settling conflicts and recall the principles of the OAU, notably Declaration No 16 of July 1964 in Cairo on the territorial integrity of states and the inviolability of borders inherited from the colonial era.
In consequence the heads of state reaffirm their commitment to the peace plan of the U.N. and OAU in the Resolution 10/97 of the Security Council of the United Nations on 18 February 1997.

The heads of state call straight away for the two parties to respect the commitments freely subscribed to in the terms of the final communique of the extraordinary summit of the OAU at Lome on the 27th of March 1997 and of the Communique of Pretoria on the 8th of April 1997.

The heads of state of Central Africa took note of the important statement made by President Mobutu Sese Seko, according to which, because of his health problems, he will not stand for re-election, also opening new prospects for a negotiated political settlement of the conflict. They seize this occasion to reaffirm their attachment to the democratic process and the putting in place of institutions.

The heads of state invite Zaire's political forces under the direction of the High Council of the Republic - Transitional Parliament to proceed with the election of its president to allow normal functioning of institutions and favour an orderly and democratic transition, conforming with the Constitutional Transition Act.

Drawing lessons from the Zairean crisis with the aim of reinforcing peace and stability in Central Africa, the heads of state have decided to set up a structure of dialogue and management of crises in Central Africa of which the structures will be arranged by the heads of state.
The heads of state have also decided to undertake mediation and peace missions to the heads of state of countries concerned with the conflict in Zaire.

Finally, the heads of state launch an emotional appeal to the parties in conflict for an immediate cessation of hostilities, to create the conditions for a negotiated political settlement of the Zairean crisis.
Libreville, 8th May 1997
